symptom: Alignment push/pop invents a fifth decryptor argument and 128-bit return (major, 1 instance, crackmes.one 67f9bdc38f555589f3530a85 WeeperVM--Level_1 sub_10e27 @0x10e27)
decisions: The filed hypothesis ('the incidental RDX value restored from an alignment slot is treated as a second return register') was already overturned by the round-12 refuter and is confirmed wrong here: the alignment SLOT is irrelevant. dead_rdx_write (mov %rdi,%rax; add $7,%rax; mov %rsi,%rdx; ret) touches no stack and shows the identical undefined16 + v._8_8_ = a1 shape. It is genuinely ambiguous (indistinguishable from a struct{long,long} return) and is deliberately left alone.

The real gate is the shipped default-ON retinputhalf (DIV-85), whose placement test -- a terminal at a DIFFERENT address than the half means the function moved the argument there -- is satisfied by an accident. The circularity is the defect proper: keeping the half is what gives R8 a reader, and R8 having a reader is what makes it a parameter.

Neither escape hatch is usable as a fix. Re-measured here: `--option retinputhalf off` turns __int128 wide_ret(long,long) into `unsigned long wide_ret(...){return a1;}` (high half silently lost); `--option returnpair single` loses a return half AND a whole parameter on struct{long,long} two_ret. Both destroy genuine 128-bit returns.

The discriminator is NOT available where the decision is made. Dumped the IR at ActionOutputPrototype for the witness, for cross_reg_restore (push %r8/pop %rdx) and for five() (mov %r8,%rdx): all three are `RDX = COPY(R8_input)` at the RETURN address, byte-for-byte identical. Copy propagation has already collapsed the store and the load, and the dead ops are gone from the optree (checked: iter_all shows 4 ops). So the evidence must be captured during the flow build.

Rule shipped: a register is push-only when some stack-adjusting instruction stores it to memory and no instruction in the function ever writes it. The write test excludes the ordinary callee-saved save/restore (the pop writes the register it pushed); the stack-adjust test excludes every genuine shape measured. Recorded in p2_lift/flow.rs (6 lines), consulted by kuna_retinputhalf::is_input_parameter.

The SLEIGH push stages the value through a unique temp (`t = COPY(R8); RSP = RSP - 8; STORE(ram,RSP,t)`), and before heritage every use is its own free Varnode, so the temp is followed by STORAGE, not by Varnode identity. That was the difference between a no-op and a working rule.

Known residual, not papered over: a function that pushes an argument register purely to preserve it across a call and pops it into a DIFFERENT register that it then returns is read as maintenance. Nothing local separates that from the alignment idiom; documented in the module header, the spec and the option's use_when.

Controls re-measured on the final build, not inherited: wide_ret keeps undefined16 with v1._8_8_ = a0 / v1._0_8_ = a1 and two_ret keeps both computed halves, so no genuine 128-bit return is touched; the three-way idiom discriminator is exact -- cross_reg_restore goes from the 5-argument undefined16 to `long sub_100a(long a0)` while same_reg_restore and dead_rdx_write are byte-identical with the option on and off.

scripts.repipe.mergecheck reports MERGE BLOCKED on this branch and the block is a structural false positive for every new-option PR, not a hazard here. All 14 rejects are shape-C `line-added-twice` on phases.toml: adding one `[[settable]]` row necessarily increments the count of each boilerplate key line (`tier = "core"`, `strength = "HARD"`, `values = "on|off"`, ...), and the multiset check cannot tell a legitimately added row from a keep-both duplicated one. Measured control: the last merged option PR, DIV-155 pdatainterior (#557) which IS origin/main, trips 11 of the identical rejects against its own parent, while its non-phases.toml predecessor 8b85b588 trips 0. The hazard shape-C actually guards is impossible here -- `line-removed` is 0 on every keepboth path and the branch is a single commit fast-forward on origin/main, so no 3-way merge and no keep-both resolution ever occurred. The guards that discriminate are all clean: shape-A confirms DIV-156 is still the next free number on origin/main and lists all 9 references as consistent, shape-B re-derives every shared counter and agrees (184 settables, tiers 57/68/59, 267 corpus files, next ElementId 4162), and docs/baseline.json is byte-identical to origin/main.
